In December, 1884, the Savoy College newspaper, its own will to the position, published a charter, published a Savoy Platonian Literary Charter from the Secretary of State:⁶⁸

We the undersigned wishing to incorporate ourselves into one body make and constitute ourselves as follows:

FIRST.

It is formed for the purpose of Literary Discussion, Political Discussion, for the purpose of forwarding the honorable aims of its members in life.

SECOND.

It shall be conducted and carried on in Savoy College, town of Savoy, County of Fannin, State of Texas.

THIRD.

It shall exist for a term of ninety-nine years and shall have power to confer degrees on its members under the supervision of its seal.

The officers of said society shall consist of President, Vice-President, Recording Secretary, Corresponding Secretary, Treasurer, and Sergeant-at-Arms.

⁶⁸This is reported to be the beginning of the Society is a letter from a Item of about March, 1886, and published in The Platonian Messenger; The No. 9, April 3, 1884; No. 4, April 15, 1885. "The [Platonian] Society exists in the College library since it was the college's own." The reference elsewhere is to the College library since it was the one in which the book is held, including as it was the actual citation.
